title: Introduction
content:
# The Quran Life Philosophy

Welcome to the **Quran Life** documentation. This application is not just a tool—it is a unified system designed for the lifelong journey of Quran memorization and maintenance.

## Beyond Rote Memorization

The core philosophy of Quran Life is to **maximize sequential Quranic verse recall with minimal cognitive effort.** 

Traditional memorization works but is not efficient due to:
1. **The Forgetting Curve**: Without structured review, what is learned is quickly lost.
2. **Cognitive Overload**: Managing what to review, when to review, and how to fix errors can become overwhelming.

Quran Life addresses these by integrating three powerful pillars:
- **Visual Memory (Mindmaps)**: Giving your brain a physical "place" to store verses.
- **Smart Review (Spaced Repetition)**: Scientifically optimized schedules to ensure long-term retention.
- **Similar Verse (Mutashabihat) Awareness**: Proactive handling of common points of confusion.

## The "Life" in Quran Life
The app is designed to be a companion for life. It handles the "administrative" side of memorization—scheduling, tracking, and error analysis—allowing you to focus entirely on the sacred words.

---

**Ready to start?** Head over to our [Getting Started Guide](/docs/philosophy/getting-started) for a step-by-step walkthrough of the app.

title: Getting Started
content:
# Welcome to Quran Life

Quran Life is more than just a tracking app—it's a complete system for memorizing the Quran using visual memory and smart scheduling. This guide will take you from your first day to mastery.

## Phase 1: Setting Up Your Territory

When you first launch the app, you'll go through an **Onboarding** process to set your initial preferences. If you ever need to adjust them, you can do so in the [Settings](/docs/philosophy/settings) tab:

1.  **Set Your Active Part**: Choose the Part (Juz) you are working on. This focuses the app's Todo list and Daily Portion on your current goal.
    - Quran Life currently uses a **7-part system** for active focus.
2.  **Skipping Surahs**: You can mark Surahs you have already fully mastered (like Surah Al-Fatiha or Al-Ikhlas) as **Skipped**. This removes them from your daily portion, todo list, and reviews to prevent cluttering your workflow with things you already know perfectly.

## Phase 2: The Daily Habit (Passive Exposure)

Every day, open the **Today** tab. Your first goal is **Passive Exposure**. This ensures that you maintain a constant relationship with the entire text you are memorizing.

-   **Listen/Read Your Portion**: This is a specific set of verses the app gives you daily. Listen to it to subconsciously absorb the verses. This builds a foundation for your active memorization while you prepare your visual mindmaps.
-   **How it's Calculated**: Your portion size is determined by your **Active Part** and your **Target Completion Days** (set in Settings). We divide the total verses by your target days to get a baseline.
-   **Goal**: The intent is to complete a full reading/listening cycle of your active territory every 7-30 days.
-   **Hafs Mushaf Standard**: We use the official **Hafs Mushaf** text and alignment to ensure your memorization matches the most widely used standard.
-   **The Blue Dot**: A small blue dot on the "Today" icon will remind you if you haven't finished your daily listening yet.
-   **Undo/Redo**: If you grade a review by mistake in Today, use undo/redo to correct it immediately.

It is recommended to move on to the **active learning phase** (marking it as complete for reviews) once you have completed enough **Daily Portion** cycles to feel the "sound" and general flow of the verses. Once you meet this criteria, you might need a tiny amount of rote repetition at the very end to bridge any final gaps before marking a Surah as fully learned. This should be quick and targeted. 

However, if you are in a rush, you can bypass the passive listening phase and use rote memorization to "cram" the verses into your short-term memory. Once you know the words, you **must still create or use pre-made mindmap** to lock them in.

## Phase 3: Active Memorization (Visual Mindmaps)

This is where the real work happens in the **Todo** tab. Instead of just repeating verses, you will associate them with a visual "map."

1.  **Choose Your Path**: For every Surah, you have two options:
    -   **Use a Pre-Made Map**: Start with the official mindmap for speed and reference.
    -   **Edit/Create Your Own**: Use the built-in drawing tools to edit the pre-made mindmap or build your own mindmap from scratch. This usually gives stronger memory because you make the structural decisions yourself.
    -   **Upload Policy**: Uploading external content is not allowed in the mindmap editor.
2.  **Setup Your Verse Groups**: If creating your own, use the **Splits configuration modal** to split the Surah into visual segments (we call these "chunks").
3.  **Complete the Map**: It is **crucial** to create or use existing mindmap before you start reviewing specific verses.
    -   *Why?* Without a visual map, your brain has no "place" to store the verses, leading to weak, isolated memories that fade quickly. The map provides the structure that holds the verses together.
4.  **Mark as Complete**: Once your map is ready and you feel familiar with the verses through your **Daily Portion** cycles, mark the Surah as complete to begin your **Smart Review** cycle.

> To help you situate yourself, we have added icons that appear directly on the Kanban cards themselves:
> - Brain: Custom mindmap (not an official template).
> - BadgeCheck: Official (pre-made) mindmap.
> - PenSquare: Official map edited by you.
> - Layers: Custom map, but an official reset is available.
> - scissors: Splits not created yet.

*Deep Dive: [How to create effective Mindmaps](/docs/philosophy/mindmap-strategy)*

## Phase 4: Long-Term Mastery (Smart Reviews)

Once you've "learned" a Surah, the app will ask you to review it periodically.

-   **When to Review**: The app uses a [Smart Review System](/docs/philosophy/spaced-repetition) to show you verses just as you're about to forget them.
-   **Today Counter**: The red badge on the "Today" tab shows high-priority reviews due or overdue.

## Maintenance: Managing Your Tasks

As you progress, the **Todo** tab will be your hub for maintenance. Watch for the **Todo Counter**, which indicates structural tasks that need attention:

-   **Memory Gaps (Suspended Verse Groups)**: If you fail a review 3 times, the app [Suspends it](/docs/philosophy/re-learning). This forces you to stop and fix your mindmap before moving on.
-   **Similar Verses (Mutashabihat)**: The app will alert you to [Similar Verses](/docs/philosophy/mutashabihat). Use logic and thematic flow to distinguish them, rather than simple tricks.

---

## Pro Tips

-   **Track Your Growth**: Check the [Statistics](/docs/philosophy/statistics) tab to see your "Memory Maturity" grow over time.

title: Mindmap Strategy
content:
# Mindmap Strategy

Mindmaps are the heart of the Quran Life strategy. They bridge the gap between abstract text and your brain's powerful spatial memory.

## Why Visual Maps Matter
Your brain is naturally wired to remember **places and pictures** much better than lists of text. By using visual maps, we reduce the mental effort needed for recall. Instead of struggling to find the next verse in a vacuum, your brain "sees" where it sits on the map you created. This helps you:
- **Create Visual Landmarks**: Tie each group of verses to a specific spot.
- **See the Big Picture**: Understand themes and how they flow into each other.
- **Build Personal Connections**: Create a stronger mental bond by arranging the map yourself.

## How it Works in the App

### 1. Two Levels of Mapping
Visual memory aids are key to long-term retention. We use two distinct levels:
- **Part Mindmap**: A high-level overview of an entire section (Part/Juz) to help you understand the core themes and flow between different Surahs. The app currently uses a 7-part structure.
- **Surah Mindmap**: A detailed visual guide for a specific Surah. You use the built-in editor to work with approved or existing mindmap content and split it into smaller, manageable segments for review.
- **Part 0 Meta Mindmap (Todo-only reference)**: The Todo Kanban includes a persistent Part 0 card that summarizes relationships across Parts 1-7. It is a reference layer and does not change when you switch Active Part.

> Mindmap editor policy: user uploads are not allowed. Do not upload any external content into the mindmap editor.

> Our Design Philosophy: These mindmaps are not meant to capture every detail, nor to serve as the only or definitive way to understand the Qur’an. They are built for one primary purpose: to help you remember. For that reason, they prioritize clarity, structure, and ease of recall over completeness. This requires intentionally limiting complexity. Mapping every logical transition would produce dense, overwhelming diagrams that make recall harder—not easier. Less is more. Moreover, many transitions are already conveyed through rhythm, sound patterns, and the natural flow of the verses, making additional visual representation unnecessary.

### 2. Splitting Verses
The core of the strategy is linking your visual map to the actual verses.
- **Split configuration modal**: This tool is used **specifically when creating or editing a mindmap**. It allows you to create "Splits" (verse chunks) that correspond to the different sections of your map.
- **Short-Surah default**: For Surahs with **10 verses or fewer**, the app automatically treats the Surah as one verse group (`1..N`) even if you did not save manual splits yet.
- **Manual override**: If you save your own splits, your saved splits immediately replace that default single-group behavior.
- **The Flow**: Your map should show the flow between different groups of verses. If you find yourself forgetting a specific group, it's a sign that your map needs more detail or that the group should be split into smaller pieces.
- **Editable Blocks**: Mindmaps are not set in stone—they should evolve as your memory deepens. On this note, the current pre-made mindmaps will receive future updates if a better, more efficient structure is found.

## Rules for Effective Mindmap Creation

For those creating mindmaps from scratch or editing pre-made ones, following these rules ensures your map is a powerful memory tool, not just a drawing.

### 1. Ask the Right Question (The Art of Chunking)
The goal is to find the most appropriate grouping structure for the topic.
-   **Hypothesis of Chunking**: Create hypotheses until you find the best fit.
-   **Group Size**: Keep groups to **2 to 4 items**. If you have more, chunk further. Small chunks help solve problems and find patterns for better retention.
-   **The Core Questions**: To form these groups, ask:
    -   *"Why is this important?"* (Intuitive chunking)
    -   *"How are they related to each other?"*
-   **Follow Curiosity**: Let your questions flow naturally from your curiosity. You will instinctively shift from the big picture to the details. However, it's important to recognize the text's superior order. Therefore, the mind map can be somewhat flexible in organization as long as it roughly follows the sequence presented by the material.
-   **Emotional Connection**: Be curious, emotional, and personal when seeking answers. Good inquiry leads to good relationships, which leads to good chunking.

### 2. Work in Layers of Information
Build your map in these distinct levels:
1. **Level 0: Big picture**: Every surah mind map should account for the part mind map it belongs to. This mainly relates to the surah's central theme, which should match the logic of the part mind map and ideally be unique.
2.  **Level 1: Logic (The Backbone):** This is the main relationship or "cause → effect." It shows the flow or transition between verse groups within the surah. An important point is that each transition always moves forward, not backward (like the ring theory), because each group must serve a unique purpose. Otherwise, the flow of memory is disrupted.
3.  **Level 2: Concepts (How and What)**: This represents the actual verse group. It should mention the number of verses it covers.
4.  **Level 3: Important Details**: These are specific details that make the concept easier to understand. They should only be fleshed out *on demand* if the concept itself isn't clear enough.

### 3. Characteristics of a High-Quality Mindmap
A good mindmap is:
-   **Visual & Non-Verbal**: Use doodles and abstract concepts with as few words as possible.
-   **Processed & Focused**: It answers the specific question you started with ("aim") and prioritizes relationships that bridge concepts rather than just tree-like lists.
-   **Reflective & Freehand**: Drawn freely using your own hand writing, preferably for better encoding. However, other tools like the "arrow" or "text" tool can be used if you don't have the necessary device (drawing tablet or mobile tablet with pen support).
-   **Grouped & Intuitive**:
    -   Use sub-chunks if there are more than 4 branches.
    -   Determine hierarchy by asking "What's most important?".
    -   Link to prior knowledge.
-   **Directional & Emphasized**: Show clear flow of information (cause → effect) and make main concepts visually obvious (size, thickness).
-   **Efficient**: Designed to be retained and applied from recall. *Skew is okay*—it's normal for some parts to be denser than others.

## How to Effectively Review Mindmaps

When your mindmaps are due for review, use the **Teach Method** to solidify your understanding. The goal is to explain the map to yourself (or an imaginary student) in this order: **Big Picture → Concept → Big Picture**.

Follow these steps for a good explanation:

-   **Seek Big Picture Relevance**: Constantly ask yourself how this part fits into the whole.
-   **Reverse Explanation**: Explain the concept *first*, then give it a name. Don't just name it and then explain it.
-   **Flexible Teaching**: Don't get locked into teaching it the same way every time. Change your approach.
-   **Speak Out Loud**: This slows you down, allowing you to explore each point fully.

## Source Transparency for Pre-Made Mindmaps

For official pre-made mindmaps, each mindmap documentation page includes a **Source Verification** section maintained by the Quran Life team.

- It lists the references used to build the map.
- It includes exact page citations for each Surah/Part.
- It is for transparency and trust, not an extra task for learners.

If you want to create or edit a mindmap faster, you can use the linked sources directly. They are selected to support thematic (**mawdou'i**) interpretation rather than detailed analytical (**tahlili**) verse-by-verse interpretation.

title: Mutashabihat
content:
# Managing Similar Verses (Mutashabihat)

**Similar Verses** (known technically as *Mutashabihat*) are verses that look or sound almost identical. They are one of the most common challenges in Quran memorization. Quran Life helps you tackle them head-on.

## Awareness During Review

To help during review, the app automatically identifies these verses and provide extra context—automatically showing more of the verse or giving hints—until the point where the similarity ends.

## How to Approach Similarities

You can handle similar verses in two main ways:

1. **Reactive (Errors during Review)**: This is the most efficient way. The app automatically flags similar verses in your **Todo** tab only when you make a mistake on a verse with a known similarity during a review. This ensures you only solve problems when they actually arise or become relevant.

2. **Proactive Study**: If you want to be thorough, you can find a complete list of all similarities for your active part in the [Settings](/docs/philosophy/settings) tab.

## The Best Way to Distinguish

When two verses are similar, it's tempting to use "tricks" (like remembering which letter comes first). However, we highly recommend using **logic**:
- **Thematic Flow**: Understand *why* a specific word is used based on the theme of the Surah. Logic is much harder to forget than a simple trick.
- **Visual Separation**: Place similar verses in different locations on your [Mindmap](/docs/philosophy/mindmap-strategy) to create a clear distinction in your mind.

## Why This Matters
By addressing similar verses explicitly, you remove the "second-guessing" that often happens during recitation. Instead of being unsure, you make a conscious decision on how to tell them apart.

title: Re-Learning
content:
# Fixing Memory Gaps (Re-learning)

Even with a perfect system, some verses will be harder to remember than others. When a specific verse chunk fails multiple times, the app moves it into a **Re-learning Phase**.

## The 3-Strike Rule

If you mark a **single verse group** as **Not Remembered** 3 times in a row, the app will:
1. **Suspend the Item**: It is removed from your daily "Today" reviews.
2. **Save your error**: It shows you the exact verse where you made the error, so you know what to focus on.

Important clarification: these 3 errors do **not** need to be in one exact verse. They can happen across different verses inside that same verse group. Suspension triggers only when all 3 errors are within one verse group.

This is a safety feature. It prevents you from wasting time on a memory that isn't sticking. Instead of repeating the same mistake, you are forced to stop and fix the underlying issue.

## How to Fix a Memory Gap

When an item is suspended, follow these steps:
- **Review Your Map**: Open your mindmap for that Surah. Is the visual flow clear?
- **Update the Map**: Often, you just need a more detailed image or a better "story" for that verse chunk.
- **Refine the Split**: Use the Splits configuration modal to split the difficult chunk into even smaller pieces, if needed.

## Why This Matters
This phase ensures you aren't just "guessing" your way through reviews. It builds a solid, error-free foundation for your memorization.

title: Settings
content:
# Managing Your Journey (Settings)

The **Settings** tab is the control center for your memorization plan. Here, you tell the app what you want to achieve and what you already know.

## Define Your Scope

- **Active Part (Juz)**: This is your current focus area. The app filters your **Todo** list and **Daily Portion** to only show Surahs within this Part. Quran Life currently uses a 7-part structure, and you can change your active part at any time as you progress.
  - **Part 0 Meta Mindmap (Todo)**: On the **Todo** page, a dedicated **Part 0 Meta Mindmap** card is always included in the Kanban to explain how Parts 1-7 relate to each other. This card stays available regardless of which Active Part you choose here.
- **Target Completion**: How many days do you want to take to finish a full cycle of listening/reading your Active Part? This setting determines the size of your **Daily Portion**. You can also reset your daily portion progress here if needed.

## Skipped Surah

This section allows you to manage Surahs you want to exclude from your daily cycle (e.g., ones you know perfectly like Al-Fatiha or don't want to review yet). You can unskip them at any time to add them back to your review queue.

## Knowledge Tracking

This section allows you to quickly check or update the maturity of Surahs or mindmaps, individually or in bulk. You can also filter by their state for quick navigation.

## Similar Coverage

This section helps you identify Surahs that contain many "Similar Verses" (Mutashabihat). You can see which ones are causing confusion and prioritize them.

## Advanced options

In this section, you can change some default behaviors of the app, such as the sorting of the kanban board or review queue, the default filter in the To-Do tab, or the default daily portion mode. You can also change what certain actions do, such as the effect of moving cards out of the "Complete" column on their related verse groups and mind maps.

title: Spaced Repetition
content:
# Smart Review System (FSRS)

Quran Life uses the advanced **FSRS (Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler)** algorithm to manage your review schedule. FSRS is a modern, data-driven system that outperforms older algorithms (like SM-2).

## How Your Brain Remembers

Memories fade over time. However, if you review information just as you are about to forget it, that memory becomes significantly stronger. FSRS calculates this "forgetting curve" precisely for every single verse group.

*Our system uses [Visual Mindmaps](/docs/philosophy/mindmap-strategy) as the primary review unit to give your brain a physical 'place' to store these memories.*

## The Review Process

The smart system schedules reviews at optimal intervals to minimize your workload while maximizing retention.

- **Step-by-Step Revelation**: Long verses are divided into smaller parts. This helps you check your recitation in small pieces, reducing the risk of missing minor errors.
- **Recall, Don't Read**: The goal is to recall the verse from memory *before* clicking to reveal it.
- **Grading Your Performance**: After revealing the verses, you have two simple choices:
    -   **Remembered**: You successfully recalled the verse. The system will increase the interval until you see it again.
    -   **Not Remembered**: You couldn't recall it or made a significant mistake. The system will show it again sooner to help you relearn it.
-   **Not Sure**: If you make a mistake but aren't sure if it was a genuine memory gap (e.g., an accidental click or distraction), use the **Not Sure** button. This postpones the review by one day, without resetting your progress entirely.

## Efficient Learning

FSRS is highly efficient. As you prove your mastery, you will see items much less often—eventually reaching a "Mastered" state where reviews occur years apart. This saves you hours of unnecessary review time in the long run.

## Why Reviews Sometimes Reset

Occasionally, a review interval might be shortened or reset. This happens to ensure your memory stays perfectly aligned with the app:
1. **Manual Changes**: If you mark a Surah as "To Learn" and then back to "Learned."
2. **Changing Verse Ranges**: If you change the start or end of a verse chunk. Because the "chunk" you memorized has changed, the app asks you to verify it again.
3. **Repeated Mistakes**: If you mark "Not Remembered" multiple times, the system will naturally show that item more frequently until you've mastered it again.

## Keyboard Shortcuts

For a faster and more focused review experience on desktop, you can use the following shortcuts:
- **Arrow Right**: Reveal the next verse chunk, or mark as **Remembered**.
- **Arrow Left**: Mark as **Not Sure** (Postpone).
- **Arrow Down**: Mark as **Not Remembered**.

## Why This Matters
Spaced repetition ensures **minimal wasted effort**. You don't spend time reviewing what you already know well, and you don't lose progress on what you've just learned. The app handles the "when", so you can focus on the "what".

title: Statistics
content:
# Tracking Your Progress (Statistics)

The **Statistics** tab gives you a bird's-eye view of your memorization journey. It's designed to show you not just *how much* you've learned, but *how well* you know it.

## Understanding Memory Strength (Maturity)

We use **Maturity Levels** to show the strength of your memory for each verse chunk. The more times you successfully remember a verse, the "more mature" it becomes:
- **New**: Recently started or recently forgotten (reviewed every 1-14 days).
- **Medium**: Starting to stick in your long-term memory (reviewed every 14-30 days).
- **Strong**: Very solid retention (reviewed every 30-90 days).
- **Mastered**: Deeply encoded; you likely only need to see these once every few months.

The legend under each chart shows you exactly how many items fall into each of these buckets.

## What You Can Track

- **Verse Chunks**: See the maturity of individual verses. You can toggle between viewing by "Chunks" (detailed) or "Surahs" (aggregated).
- **Surah Mindmaps**: Track which Surahs have completed mindmaps and how mature those visual memories are.
- **Part Mindmaps**: A high-level view of your "Global" maps for entire Parts (Juz).
- **Daily Portion**: Shows your progress through your listening/reading cycles (how many Surahs completed vs. remaining in the current cycle).
- **Similar Verses (Mutashabihat)**: Tracks how many "Similar Verse" confusion points you have resolved (via Notes or Mindmaps) versus those still pending.
- **Review Plan**: Forecasts your review load over time and includes a **Daily Load** reference line to help you see whether upcoming days are above or below your target pace.
- **Daily Reviews**: A 180-day heatmap showing review consistency by day. It includes **Avg/Day** as a summary of your recent review rhythm.
- **Weak Surahs**: Highlights Surahs with the highest **mistake counts** in the selected range. It counts both **mindmap** and **verse-group** review errors for each Surah.

## Accuracy & Filters
To give you the most accurate picture, the statistics are filtered by your **Active Part** and automatically exclude any Surahs you've marked as **Skipped** in the Settings.
